title: webhook.v1
description: The outbound webhook wire shape: the delivery envelope POSTed to a subscriber's URL, plus the signed-header scheme that authenticates it. Two producers share it. Subscription deliveries (the /v2/webhooks subscribers, §2.7) are MeetingEvent and TestEvent envelopes: meeting-api's status writer stores each event in webhook_outbox (intake/status.py, intake/outbox.py) and webhooks/sender.py posts the stored body, signed under the subscriber's secret. Legacy deliveries (the system hook and a meeting's per-user webhook_url) are built by lifecycle/webhook.py and posted by webhooks/delivery.py. Every delivery of either producer is an Envelope.

EventType.description: The webhook event types this contract delivers. meeting.* mirror the meeting FSM (lifecycle.v1) plus the intake.v1 entry lifecycle (scheduled/updated/removed/waiting_for_room/not_sent); recording.* / transcription.* are post-meeting artifacts; export.* is the exporter's handoff result; webhook.test is an on-demand subscriber test send; bot.retry is reserved for the lobby-timeout retry, not yet emitted.

Envelope.description: The outer shape of every delivery, subscription or legacy. The body POSTed to the subscriber is the serialised Envelope; the HMAC signs `"<timestamp>." + body`. A subscription delivery is also a MeetingEvent or a TestEvent, which pin its data. A legacy delivery's data is `{ meeting, status_change? }`, with the legacy meeting block (integer id plus uuid).

event_id.description: stable identity of the logical event; delivery is at-least-once and the receiver dedupes on this key. The SAME logical event carries the SAME event_id across every (re)delivery. Subscription: `evt_` + sha256 hex of `<meeting id>|<event_type>|<sequence>` (webhook.test: `evt_test_` + 32 random hex). Legacy: `evt_` + the first 32 hex of sha256 of `<connection_id>|<event_type>|<new_status>`. See the webhook.v1 README 'Delivery semantics'.

created_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp the envelope was built

data.description: event-type-specific body, kept open here. Subscription deliveries: see MeetingEvent and TestEvent. Legacy deliveries: `{ meeting: {...}, status_change?: {...} }`.

Change.description: The status step a subscription meeting event records (§2.7). `from` is null on a meeting's first event (it came into being in `to`); `reason` is the step's reason when it has one; `at` is the whole-second UTC instant of the step.

MeetingEvent.description: A subscription delivery of a meeting event (§2.7): every event type except webhook.test. One event per meeting step, stored by the status writer (meeting_api.intake.status) in webhook_outbox and posted as stored by webhooks/sender.py. data.meeting is the intake.v1 Meeting (the §2.4 projection: UUID id, sequence). data.change is present on every status change and on meeting.scheduled. data.merged_into is present only on a meeting.removed that merged the meeting into a live one.

event_id.description: `evt_` + sha256 hex of `<data.meeting.id>|<event_type>|<data.meeting.sequence>`: the same on every redelivery, distinct for every event of a meeting

created_at.description: whole-second UTC instant the event was recorded

merged_into.description: the id (UUID) of the live meeting this one was merged into

TestEvent.description: A subscription test send (§2.7, POST /v2/webhooks/{id}/test): stored by meeting_api.intake.outbox.PostgresWebhookTests and posted, signed, to that one subscriber. It carries no meeting.

event_id.description: `evt_test_` + 32 random hex, one per test send

SignatureHeaders.description: The headers a verifier recomputes to authenticate a delivery. The signature is `sha256=<hex(hmac_sha256(secret, "<X-Webhook-Timestamp>." + raw_body))>`. X-Webhook-Timestamp bounds replay. Subscription deliveries always carry them and never carry Authorization. Legacy deliveries carry them only when the per-user webhook_secret is set, with Authorization alongside.

X-Webhook-Timestamp.description: unix seconds the signature was computed at (replay window)

X-Webhook-Signature-Previous.description: sha256=<hmac under the previous secret>: subscription deliveries only, during the 24h after a rotate-secret call; a receiver accepts a match on either signature header

Authorization.description: Bearer <secret>: legacy per-user deliveries only, alongside the HMAC. Subscription deliveries never carry it.
